name: n1_nde_t2
headline: AI Generated
windows: The closest thing I can compare it to is the out-of-body part of some near-death experiences.

People sometimes report seeing things from impossible angles, and some of those reports (controversially) were verified by others in the room. My room event had nothing like that to check, though, since I wasn’t floating around noticing any details. So those cases can’t back mine up. They just help me show what I mean by an experience that wasn’t stuck at the body’s vantage point anymore. If you want to go down that rabbit hole, there’s this systematic analysis of near-death reports, the AWARE-II cardiac-arrest study, and a recent veridical-NDE evidence scale.

name: n1_percentages_t2
headline: Human Written
windows: This distinction isn’t laid out explicitly in the suttas. AN 11.12 says a noble disciple can reach ease and joy through recollecting the Buddha, Dhamma, & Saṅgha – the community of realized disciples – or recollecting ethical conduct, generosity, or qualities shared with heavenly beings.

In my experience there can also be physical loosening of unification. My percentages are just a playful way of saying how much binding has dissolved. Around 1%, a person can still do everything fine. Around 5%, they can hardly do anything.
(And partial untying goes beyond that range too.)

name: n1_burden_t2
headline: AI Generated
windows: In SN 22.22 the Buddha puts the weight in one place and the carrying in another. The five aggregates are the burden, and craving is what picks it up. The tangle is heavy all by itself (even an arahant still feels the first dart), and craving is why we keep lugging it around. Physics backs this up, and I mean literally: quarks supply less than 1% of a proton’s mass, and roughly 99% comes from gluon-binding energy.
Matter weighs what its binding weighs.

name: n1_diamond_t2
headline: AI Generated
windows: I used to attribute “life is like a dream” directly to the historical Buddha.

The famous stanza I loved is actually from the later Mahāyāna Diamond Sutra, which puts some words in his mouth. The early Pāli texts were already reaching for the same kind of pictures, though. In SN 22.95 form is like foam, feeling is like a bubble, perception is a mirage and consciousness is a magic trick, and Dhammapada 170 tells us to look at the world like a bubble, or a mirage.

name: n1_driving_t2
headline: AI Detected
windows: My buddy E. told me he had much stronger episodes while driving: for long stretches, his own car and the traffic seemed to disappear.
He never had an accident either.

Whether that was luck, or he got it wrong about what was happening, or it’s something about how these states work, or some mix of those, God only knows.
Either way, I wouldn’t keep driving through that myself. If you’re having episodes like that, I’d stay away from driving or running machinery until you understand them better.
